title: Best Stock Profit
prompt: A stock practice app receives one price per day. Write a function that returns the maximum profit from buying once and selling later. Return 0 when no profitable trade exists.

explanation.beginner:
Example: maxProfit([7,1,5,3,6,4]) produces 5. Track the cheapest earlier buying price and the best profit so far. A candidate sale must use an earlier buy, then update the running minimum.

Compare “returns 0 for decreasing prices”: input [[9,7,4,1]] produces 0. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Track the cheapest earlier buying price and the best profit so far. A candidate sale must use an earlier buy, then update the running minimum.

Tempting mistake: Subtracting the global minimum from the global maximum ignores whether buying happened before selling.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated. One pass costs O(n) time and O(1) additional space.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns 0 for decreasing prices”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
